Astronomers Create Largest 2D Map of the Universe with 5.6 Trillion Pixels

2026-08-12 Samantha Mathewson 2D map, universe, DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, NOIRLab, cosmic cartography, astronomy, 4 billion objects, 5.6 trillion pixels
Read the source article

Quick summary

Astronomers have released the largest 2D map of the universe ever created, charting nearly 4 billion cosmic objects across 5.6 trillion pixels, culminating 13 years of observations from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys.

Key takeaways

  • Largest 2D map of the universe charts nearly 4 billion cosmic objects in 5.6 trillion pixels
  • Represents 13 years of observations and data processing from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
  • Data collected from telescopes at Kitt Peak National Observatory and Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory
  • Previous versions of the dataset have been referenced in over 1,800 scientific papers
  • The map serves as a pointer for other telescopes and supports DESI's dark energy spectroscopic survey
  • Could help train AI systems to analyze data from next-generation observatories
